purpose: Current brief coverage, with implementation evidence and explicit remaining account/runtime boundaries. Delivered means the repository feature, not legal certification, programme approval or measured outcomes.
rule: Status is a claim about this repository, so each one is checkable: the 'where' paths must exist in the tree (the build fails if one does not), the evidence links open the file or the official page that settles it, and a row with no evidence must be a row whose honest answer is that nothing exists yet.

status_legend.delivered: Implemented and visible on the published site.
status_legend.partial: Implemented in part. The gap is named on the row.
status_legend.blocked: Cannot be done from outside Amazon's own systems. No amount of work here closes it.
status_legend.not_delivered: Buildable today with the inputs already present, and not built yet.

counts_note: Counts are computed from the rows at build time rather than typed, so this page cannot claim a total the register does not contain.

requirements.requirement: Actually generate organic traffic

The site is technically indexable but nothing has been submitted to any search engine, no page has an inbound link, the domain is a github.io project subpath rather than a domain the owner controls, and there is no analytics to tell whether a single visitor arrives. Publishing a sitemap is a precondition for organic traffic, not a cause of it.

requirements.requirement: Catchy, trendy articles that a shopper would actually read
requirements.clause: It should include catchy trendy articles and topics related to the product we are promoting.

evidence.label: article index (row count shown on the page)

requirements.why: {n_articles} articles are published and {n_topics_minus_articles} more topics are specified but unwritten. They are written to answer a question that a listing cannot ('Two 3-quart drawers or one 8-quart basket: which actually feeds four people?'), which is the durable form of 'trendy' — but they are deliberately not trend-chasing, because a trending topic has no official source and this site will not publish a claim it cannot cite. {n_articles} articles as this register was last updated, three of them added by pass 13 on 2026-11-17 with the shapes a shopper actually types: 'Chefman vs. Emeril: what a basket brand and an oven brand actually publish', '“98% less oil” is a sentence on a box, not a measurement', and 'Eight questions to ask before you buy a multi-function kitchen appliance'. Trendy in the durable sense — a question with a documented answer and a visible gap where there is none — and deliberately not trend-chasing: a trending claim with no official source is the one thing this build will not publish. What is still missing is not titles, it is cadence and query data (Q-31, Q-36, SG-43).

requirements.requirement: Resolve the three supplied links to identified products

The candidate ASINs are published and labelled unconfirmed; the owner's confirmation is the only thing that closes this.
